title: 通胀粘性不足？摩根大通：工资涨不动是关键
speaker: Bloomberg

segments.en: So, what's your take on this bang-and-line CPI print?
segments.zh: 那么，你对这次CPI数据有何看法？

segments.en: You could see under the hood there's disinflation coming from energy, and there's some inflationary pressure coming from housing and elsewhere.
segments.zh: 表面之下，能源价格带来通缩压力，而住房等领域存在通胀压力。

segments.en: Well, first of all, when you look at an employment reporter, CPI report, the truth is CPI is almost always about the analysts think, because we have a lot of data going into it,
segments.zh: 首先，看CPI报告时，实际上它几乎总是与分析师的预期一致，因为已有大量数据。

segments.en: which just makes it very hard to have a big surprise. So, not surprise, that we're not surprised.
segments.zh: 因此很难出现大的意外，所以我们不感到意外并不奇怪。

segments.en: Having said that, I think there is a clear disinflationary trend.
segments.zh: 尽管如此，我认为存在明显的通缩趋势。

segments.en: There are a lot of cross-currents, a lot of cross-waves in the day to this morning, things like airline fare is up, but tobacco prices, not moving as much as it did last month,
segments.zh: 今天早间数据中有许多交叉波动，比如机票价格上涨，但烟草价格涨幅不如上月。

segments.en: the differences in medical commodities and services.
segments.zh: 医疗商品和服务也存在差异。

segments.en: But beneath it all, I think there are a few things to bear in mind. One, we're going to have lower tariff costs going forward that we've had a year ago, because the new tariffs
segments.zh: 但总体来看，有几点值得注意：未来关税成本将低于一年前，因为新关税不会完全取代原有关税。

segments.en: are not going to fully replace the AEPA tariffs. Second, I do think that eventually oil price will come down, because eventually, there's only one solution to this thing,
segments.zh: 其次，我认为油价最终会下跌，因为最终只有一个解决方案。

segments.en: and everybody's always going to get out of the straight of our moves, and I think it will.
segments.zh: 每个人都会摆脱当前的困境，我相信会如此。

segments.en: But the biggest thing to me is, this is the fourth consecutive month in which wages have gone up by less than CPI inflation.
segments.zh: 但对我来说最重要的是，这是工资涨幅连续第四个月低于CPI通胀。
工资同比上涨3.2%，CPI同比上涨3.4%。

segments.en: And what that tells me is American workers can't get a raise.
segments.zh: 这告诉我，美国工人无法获得加薪。

segments.en: And if they can't, you cannot have sticky inflation. We've essentially got Teflon inflation in America.
segments.zh: 如果他们不能，你就不会有粘性通胀。我们基本上在美国有了特氟龙通胀。

segments.en: It won't stick, and it won't stick because you can't get a price-wage spar or go, and if the wages won't react.
segments.zh: 它不会粘住，因为它不会粘住，因为你无法得到价格-工资螺旋，如果工资不反应。
